display_name: Nonna, mother of Gregory the Theologian

names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 5 august, «Sfânta Nona, mama Sfântului Grigorie Teologul», with the rank word left off.
Read out of saint.gr's line for 5 Αυγούστου, «Αγία Νόννα», with the rank word left off.

Read out of the Ohrid Prologue’s fourth heading for the Julian 5 August, „Св. Нона.“ — Св. left off, which is not a rank and gives no type. The heading is that word and her name and nothing else, so the form is the bare name; the corpus’s own display name carries «mother of Gregory the Theologian», which is the corpus’s and not this book’s. `.tmp/sr-foldpred.mjs` reports it folds with nothing.

death.note: doxologia.ro gives no year for her repose, only that it followed her husband's death: «După moartea soțului ei, în anul 374, Sfânta Nona s-a îmbolnăvit, dar a suferit această ultimă încercare spre slava lui Dumnezeu. Și-a dat sufletul ei în mâinile Domnului, în timpul slujirii dumnezeieștii Liturghii.»

attestations.note: Not checked: days.pravoslavie.ru for the corresponding Julian day (24 September 2026).

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 5 august — «Sfânta Nona, mama Sfântului Grigorie Teologul»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 5ης Αυγούστου — «Αγία Νόννα»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 5 Αυγούστου εκάστου έτους», the same day the folder's Romanian row already carries, and it is the same woman: wife of Gregory, whom the page cross-references to 1 Ιανουαρίου, and mother of Gregory the Theologian (25 Ιανουαρίου), of Caesarius (9 Μαρτίου) and of a daughter Gorgonia. saint.gr gives her repose as «πιθανώς το 374 μ.Χ.» — probably 374 — where the folder's `dates`, from the Romanian pass, read `after 374` with no upper bound; the two are compatible and the row changes nothing about them, but the Greek page's «probably» is worth the writer's eye and is in the report. The page says her husband had fallen into the heresy of the Hypsistarians, who received the Most High as of one person and did not believe in His being Trinity, and that she brought him back by her prayers and her patience. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence on the life page. The page prints no apolytikion and no kontakion, so no hymn is added.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 18.08.2026 (5. август ст. ст.) — „Св. Нона.“

attestations.note: The day’s fourth and last entry, four sentences, and the Romanian and Greek both keep her on this same 5/8. Her row was `undocumented`. **TWO BOOKS, ONE YEAR, AND THEY DISAGREE ABOUT WHOSE DEATH IT IS — AND THE INTERVAL THE FOLDER ALREADY HOLDS COVERS BOTH READINGS, SO NOTHING IS WRITTEN.** „Представила се мирно као ђакониса 374. год.“ — she reposed peacefully as a deaconess in 374 — makes the 374 **her own** death. The folder’s `dates` note records that doxologia makes the same 374 **her husband’s** death and puts hers after it, which is why the stored interval is `earliest` 374 with `latest` null and the display «after 374». **The Prologue’s reading is the earliest point of that interval and is therefore already inside it**, so narrowing it to a flat 374 would be preferring this book to the other on a question neither settles, and opening it further is not possible: an interval open at the top already holds everything. Untouched, and the disagreement is here and in the life where a reader can see it. **THE RANK IN THE BODY IS ONE THE VOCABULARY HAS, AND IT IS STILL REFUSED.** „Представила се мирно као ђакониса 374. год.“ calls her a ђакониса, and `deaconess` is in §9’s list — but ђакониса is **in the body and not in the heading**, and „Св. Нона.“ is Св. and the bare name and nothing else. The Julian 27 June ruling refuses a body rank word, so `types` stays at `righteous`, which is what the Romanian «Sfânta Nona» and the Greek «Αγία Νόννα» gave it. **This is the clearest case the wave has produced of the heading-or-body question costing a type the corpus could have expressed**, as against the two myrrh-bearers it has no word for at all, and it is named in the findings for that reason. **NO `related` ROW ADDED, AND HER HUSBAND IS THE REASON ONE COULD NOT BE.** „Мајка св. Григорија Богослова.“ and „Молитвом је св. Нона спасла од буре и свога сина Григорија Богослова.“ are her son, and `gregory-the-theologian` is `related` here already and in both directions. „Тако молитвом својом к Богу обратила је мужа свога из незнабожачке глупости у веру хришћанску.“ and „Муж њен Григорије доцније би епископом у граду Назијанзу.“ are her husband, whom her prayer turned from heathen folly to the Christian faith and who later became bishop in the city of Nazianzus: **`ls saints | grep -i nazianz` returns nothing and no folder in this corpus holds Gregory the Elder**, so Ruling 3 names him here and writes nothing. `basil-the-great` and `john-chrysostom`, the folder’s other two rows, are not in this entry at all. No `locations`: Nazianzus is her husband’s see and not a place stated of her. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion: the day carries the verse only, which is Bishop Nikolai’s own and belongs to no person.
